label: station
note: IP-neutral. A space station you fly to, land in and walk round, built from this file alone (src/systems/world/station_hull.gd draws every box from these numbers, src/systems/world/space_station.gd is the node). It is a component: it is not part of any planet. Where it hangs is a 'kind': 'station' landmark naming this file ('station': 'orbital_station'), today over the top of the ringed giant (content/core/planets/ringed_giant.json), where its deck town was; it started over the moon's far side (grit_station.json, 'side': 'far'). Take that landmark out and the station is gone; put it in another planet's landmarks and it is there instead. The plan it follows is docs/station/nitrogen_belt_plan.svg (issue #311): two towers of tall round floors, the top floor the biggest, open space between floors, an elevator up the middle in a glass tube, tunnels between the towers and a covered landing bay. The markets, homes and engine deck are furnished by 'fill' (#315, src/systems/world/station_fill.gd); the top floor and the outpost are still empty shells (#314). Its own frame: y up (level, with its own gravity, like the cruiser), x and z across, the main tower's middle at x = z = 0, y = 0 the market floor (and the bay's deck). Metres.
floors_note: Each tower is a stack of round floors (y: the top of its floor plate, radius: its outer glass wall). The space between one floor's ceiling and the next floor's plate is open to space, crossed only by the glass tube round the elevator. 'rooms': rooms round the outside behind an inner wall with doors, cut by corridors where tunnels leave; false: open from the walkway to the glass (markets). The gap in the middle of each floor (gap_radius) has a glass floor, so you look down the tube through every floor below; the elevator shaft (shaft_radius) runs up its middle, and two bridges join it to the walkway, north-south on one floor, east-west on the next.
fill_note: Issue #315: what is in the floors (src/systems/world/station_fill.gd, the render rules in docs/station/STATION_FILL.md). Each floor id with a 'use' is dressed: favela (the lower homes: rings of shacks, booths and the town's huts packed back to back at r metres, doors facing in or out, depth and h ranges in metres, booth_share/hut_share/stack_share of the pieces, alleys radial alleys alley_half wide and lane_half to the tunnel doors kept clear, lines_per_ring cables and washing lines over each alley), suites (the upper homes: every room a big suite dressed like the cantina's club and the barge), homes (the floor's open_rooms are furnished studios, the rest locked: lounge_at and kitchen_at are fractions of the way from the door to the window, partition_from_window and bed_from_window metres), market (rings of stalls at r metres from the tower's middle, every_m apart round the ring, facing in or out, huts in every other spot of a ring with huts: true (hut_h: the heights they take, a few so they share materials), or a packed ring of shacks and booths like the favela's with pack: true; nothing within lane_half metres of a tunnel door's line), engines (its rooms by turn). A floor's fill is built budget_ms a physics tick (merging merge_verts vertices at a time), and drawn only while the camera is within show_dy metres of its height and show_m of its glass. A floor's 'rooms' may be a count: the suites' floor has 10, of which the two either side of its tunnel's corridor have no door, so 8 suites; the favela's floor has none (it is open from the walkway to the glass).

hatch.note: A hatch in the middle of every tunnel's roof, closed by a shield the air cannot pass and you can: jump up through it (the jetpack) and walk the roof between its railings, out in space, like a bridge; drop back through it to get in.

tunnels_note: Enclosed glass-walled tunnels between two towers ('to': a tower id) at a level both have, or from a tower to the bay ('to': 'bay') at the bay's deck.

elevator.note: A platform rides each tower's shaft, stopping at every floor for wait seconds, at speed m/s between. Stand on it and it carries you on to the next floor the way it is going (turning at the ends); walk onto a floor's bridges while it is elsewhere and it comes to you. The shaft's doors open only on the floor where it has stopped.

bay.note: The covered landing bay: round, the port pit's size (76 m across), its deck level with y = 0, on the far side of 'from' tower's bay tunnel. Its curved wall is open at the back (the tunnel's door) and across mouth_deg of its far side (the mouth, facing away from the tower), closed by a curved energy shield along the wall's line that ships fly through and you cannot walk through. Pads: 'at' is [out toward the mouth, across] in metres from the bay's middle; every ship sits nose out to space.

dock.note: Z within radius metres flies you in: round the towers (over_y above or under_y below them, in the station's frame) when you start behind the bay's mouth, out to approach metres off the mouth at hold_y over the deck, in through the shield and to a stop over the dock pad, then turned nose out and set down (ShipPilot's docking autopilot, the same flight as the cruiser's).

outside.note: Where the planet's air is breathable (no harmful_surface, the ringed giant) the station is open to it (SpaceStation.open_air): the bay's shield lets you walk out of the mouth onto the apron, and you can roam outside on the jetpack. Over a gas ball's clouds, drop more than drop_below metres under the lowest floor and you are pulled back into the bay (lines.fell_clouds). Where you cannot breathe it is sealed as before: the shield holds you in and falling out pulls you straight back (lines.fell).
